name: teamwork-task
description: Fetch Teamwork.com tasklist/task by URL, implement each task in the current repo, commit per task using TYPE(scope): Message convention, and log time back to Teamwork. For tasklist URLs the skill filters tasks down to the ones in one of the start columns ('Ready for Development' or 'To Do' by default, case-sensitive; a task not on the board is not implemented) AND assigned to the current user — every other task is still analysed and discussed, but skipped from actual implementation (so a Laravel-backend developer working on a multi-repo project does not accidentally implement the iOS / Ionic teammate's tasks). Single-task URLs bypass the filter on purpose (a completed task is only processed after the user confirms). v1.4.0: parent tasks with subtasks are expanded into a flat working list — each subtask is fetched, planned, implemented, committed, board-moved (In progress → done column) and time-logged independently, exactly like a standalone task; the same 'start column + assigned to me' filter applies per-subtask. Pulls task attachments and comments, scans the local working tree for unattached specs/samples (e.g. `Strečnianska/DNR.docx`), pauses with a question when a task explicitly says it needs an external input that is not yet available, auto-moves the task across the board (In progress → Done - Local, with fallbacks Internal testing → Testing for older boards), gates risky commits for review, and writes sequential time logs that pick up where your last Teamwork timelog ended. v1.5.0: every task is planned, built and self-checked against five build-time quality dimensions — UI/UX & accessibility, performance, security, page reachability (a new screen ships with its menu entry and inbound links in the same commit) and framework best practices (new or changed code uses the current idioms of the framework / language versions the project actually has installed, detected from its lock files and looked up in current docs, within the project's conventions and without drive-by rewrites) — and the newest task comment is always read (full thread when the description is thin). When the companion `teamwork-task-test` plugin is installed, auto-invokes it at the end of the run (handing over any open quality items) so each task's acceptance criteria get individually verified before push. v1.6.0: work modes — `--mode=build|harden`, the `mode` config key, or the project's `.claude/wame-mode.local.md` (plugin `wame-work-mode`); `build` switches the quality dimensions, the test proposal, per-task tests and Pint, browser checks and the QA handoff off at once and records the skipped checks in `.claude/wame-deferred.local.md` for one `/wame-harden` pass; browser runners (Playwright / Puppeteer / Dusk) are never installed for a single run — a missing one is asked about once and then installed permanently.
